title: What Is AI
content: Artificial Intelligence is the science of building systems that perform tasks requiring human-like intelligence: perception, reasoning, learning, decision-making. KEY CONCEPTS: Narrow AI (task-specific, today's reality) vs General AI (human-level, not yet achieved). Symbolic AI (rules/logic) vs Machine Learning (learning from data). title: History & Paradigms
content: AI evolved through waves: symbolic/expert systems (1950s-80s), machine learning (1990s-2010s), deep learning (2010s+), foundation models/LLMs (2020s). KEY CONCEPTS: AI winters (funding collapses when hype outran results). The shift from hand-coded rules to learned patterns. WORKED EXAMPLE: Chess (rules-based Deep Blue 1997) vs Go (learned AlphaGo 2016) shows the paradigm shift. PRACTICE: 1) Map the 4 waves. 2) Explain why deep learning succeeded where rules failed.

LEARNING OBJECTIVES: Define ai agents; explain its mechanism; apply it to a realistic problem; measure or evaluate the result; identify assumptions, limitations, failure modes, security or governance implications, and connections to prior lessons.

CONCEPT: AI Agents is taught as a progressively applied competency. Identify the objective, inputs, mechanism, outputs, constraints, and evidence. Distinguish established facts from inference and forecasts. At higher levels, compare alternative methods and justify the selected approach.

METHOD: Define the problem -> establish a baseline -> gather reliable inputs -> apply the method -> calculate or observe the result -> test assumptions -> compare alternatives -> document limitations -> measure the real outcome -> revise.

WORKED APPLICATION: A small organization faces a decision involving ai agents. The learner constructs a baseline, identifies the variables that matter, chooses a method consistent with the evidence, and records both expected and actual outcomes. Where computation is relevant, show the formula, algorithm, query, or system flow rather than reporting an unexplained answer.
